headline: Larry Fink, chief executive of BlackRock, the world's largest asset manager, says any halt on data center building in the US would push the economy into recession.
score_reason: Stays at the pool score: a major financial figure, interview on 14 Oct 2026, though it is one executive's view.
importance_line: Workers in construction, energy and technology, and anyone exposed to a downturn, could be affected if building slowed, but this is one executive's forecast, not a measured estimate.
summary: CoinDesk reports on Larry Fink's CNBC interview of 14 Oct 2026, in which the BlackRock chief executive said "a moratorium of some sort in this country" would put the US in a recession because "so much of our economy is based on the buildout of this capex" (spending on new buildings and equipment). He called most fears about data centers "misinformation", while Moody's estimates planned US data center spending at $700 billion this year.
